children: Oil prices rose early Thursday as supply disruption concerns mounted following the latest flare-up in Middle East tensions, while government bonds retreated on disappointment over the U.S. Treasury Department's latest debt buyback plan.

American forces destroyed 10 Iranian tankers over the past week, the U.S. Central Command said on social media platform X. These vessels were part of a multibillion-dollar shadow network that finances the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the Central Command added.

On Wednesday, U.K. Maritime Trade Operations, or UKMTO, which is affiliated with the Royal Navy, said it had received reports of several merchant ships struck in the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of ​Oman, which are located on either side of the Strait of Hormuz.
Tehran has said it would act against threats and has announced plans for a new "exclusion zone" around the approaches to [the Strait of] Hormuz, where Iran would seek to restrict shipping.
"This battle will continue," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Wednesday. The strait is a key waterway through which one-fifth of the world's oil is transported.
Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures climbed 0.5% to $96.52 a barrel, while front-month Brent crude oil futures edged 0.1% higher to $101.32 a barrel, according to ICE data.

Meanwhile, sovereign bond prices across Asia-Pacific were weighed by disappointment over the U.S. Treasury Department's announcement that it would repurchase up to $6 billion of longer-term debt at a buyback operation on Thursday.

"Higher oil prices and disappointment around the buyback announcement pushed bond yields higher," said Sally Auld, group chief economist at National Australia Bank. "The scale of the expanded operation appeared to disappoint the market," Auld added.

Yields on Japan's 10-year government bonds rose 3.5 basis points to 2.915%, Australia's 10-year sovereign debt added 6 basis points to 5.2740%, and New Zealand's 10-year government securities gained 8 basis points to 4.8730%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.
Equity markets in Asia were lower, with South Korea's Kospi recently down 1.7%, Japan's Nikkei Stock Average falling 1.2%, and Singapore's FTSE Straits Times Index losing 0.5%.
